subject: physical-education
unit_title: Skill Assessment, Safety, and Personal Goals
title: Launch and diagnostic: movement readiness
essential_question: How can understanding skill assessment, safety, and personal goals help us explain, decide, create, or solve something that matters?
learning_objectives: Activate prior knowledge about movement readiness, surface initial thinking without penalty, and establish the unit question.
Use subject-appropriate evidence or representation to communicate understanding of movement readiness.
Check, revise, or improve work about movement readiness using stated success criteria.
success_criteria: The learner completes the central task about movement readiness.
The learner gives evidence, reasoning, a model, or a documented process rather than an unsupported answer.
The learner checks or revises the work and can identify a next step.
materials: unit-specific source, model, manipulatives, safe materials, or approved digital tool

lesson_flow.teacher_or_tutor_action: Present a brief, accessible prompt connected to “movement readiness.” Ask the learner to notice, predict, estimate, recall, or pose a question before instruction.

Prepare the body, demonstrate the skill, practice at adjustable challenge levels, use safe feedback, and cool down with reflection. Keep the explanation centered on movement readiness. Name the success criteria and model how to check work or evidence.
Complete two supported examples or source-based tasks about movement readiness. After each step, ask: “What evidence or reasoning supports that move?” Fade prompts on the second example.
Learner completes a new application of movement readiness and records both the result and the reasoning, evidence, process, or design choice that produced it.
In one concise response, show or explain the most important idea about movement readiness; then identify one check that would catch an error or weak claim.

student_activity: Learner completes a new application of movement readiness and records both the result and the reasoning, evidence, process, or design choice that produced it.
formative_check: In one concise response, show or explain the most important idea about movement readiness; then identify one check that would catch an error or weak claim.
answer_or_scoring_guidance: Score the stated learning target, accuracy, evidence/reasoning, and revision. Accept multiple valid approaches when they meet the criteria. Do not infer effort, motivation, diagnosis, or character from an error.

adaptive_tutor_routes.action: Return to the smallest prerequisite needed for movement readiness, model it with a concrete or text-only representation, then retry one fresh item.
Ask the learner to explain or represent why the process for movement readiness works before continuing.
Confirm the reasoning specifically, offer one varied example of movement readiness, and avoid unnecessary remediation.
Name the observable pattern neutrally, contrast it with a worked example, and schedule a short same-day or next-session review.
Require accurate independent application plus explanation on a later or different occasion before marking movement readiness mastered.

mastery_rule: Do not mark mastery from one answer. Use safe participation, skill cues, personal progress, strategy use, and self-assessment without body-size scoring; require accurate independent evidence and successful transfer or retrieval on at least two occasions when feasible.
extension: Apply movement readiness under a new constraint, compare two approaches or perspectives, or teach the idea with an original example without completing another learner’s graded work.
accessibility_and_accommodations: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, manipulatives-based, or demonstrated responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode.
safety_and_privacy: Use respectful, non-shaming language.
Allow a pause, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Check space, footwear, surface, weather, and equipment before movement.
Stop for pain, dizziness, breathing difficulty, head impact, or unsafe conditions and tell an adult.
Score skill, strategy, consistency, and reflection—not body size, weight, speed alone, or comparison with others.

media.suggestion: Optional diagram, map, worked example, source image, demonstration, or short clip supporting movement readiness.
media.fallback: Provide the same information as readable steps, alt text, transcript, tactile/concrete model, or teacher demonstration.

parent_or_guardian_visibility: Share the lesson target, completion state, evidence type, and next instructional step. Do not expose raw private reflections, raw answers, voice recordings, or diagnosis language. For safety-critical tasks, record only the needed guardian confirmation.
home_connection: Invite the learner to notice one safe, optional example of movement readiness in daily life. No purchase, account creation, photograph, or private disclosure is required.

essential_question: How can understanding skill assessment, safety, and personal goals help us explain, decide, create, or solve something that matters?
learning_objectives: Use error evidence to choose a different representation or strategy for skill cue review, then demonstrate corrected understanding.
Use subject-appropriate evidence or representation to communicate understanding of skill cue review.
Check, revise, or improve work about skill cue review using stated success criteria.
success_criteria: The learner completes the central task about skill cue review.
The learner gives evidence, reasoning, a model, or a documented process rather than an unsupported answer.
The learner checks or revises the work and can identify a next step.
materials: unit-specific source, model, manipulatives, safe materials, or approved digital tool

lesson_flow.teacher_or_tutor_action: Present a brief, accessible prompt connected to “skill cue review.” Ask the learner to notice, predict, estimate, recall, or pose a question before instruction.

Prepare the body, demonstrate the skill, practice at adjustable challenge levels, use safe feedback, and cool down with reflection. Keep the explanation centered on skill cue review. Name the success criteria and model how to check work or evidence.
Complete two supported examples or source-based tasks about skill cue review. After each step, ask: “What evidence or reasoning supports that move?” Fade prompts on the second example.
Learner completes a new application of skill cue review and records both the result and the reasoning, evidence, process, or design choice that produced it.
In one concise response, show or explain the most important idea about skill cue review; then identify one check that would catch an error or weak claim.

student_activity: Learner completes a new application of skill cue review and records both the result and the reasoning, evidence, process, or design choice that produced it.
formative_check: In one concise response, show or explain the most important idea about skill cue review; then identify one check that would catch an error or weak claim.
answer_or_scoring_guidance: Score the stated learning target, accuracy, evidence/reasoning, and revision. Accept multiple valid approaches when they meet the criteria. Do not infer effort, motivation, diagnosis, or character from an error.

adaptive_tutor_routes.action: Return to the smallest prerequisite needed for skill cue review, model it with a concrete or text-only representation, then retry one fresh item.
Ask the learner to explain or represent why the process for skill cue review works before continuing.
Confirm the reasoning specifically, offer one varied example of skill cue review, and avoid unnecessary remediation.
Name the observable pattern neutrally, contrast it with a worked example, and schedule a short same-day or next-session review.
Require accurate independent application plus explanation on a later or different occasion before marking skill cue review mastered.

mastery_rule: Do not mark mastery from one answer. Use safe participation, skill cues, personal progress, strategy use, and self-assessment without body-size scoring; require accurate independent evidence and successful transfer or retrieval on at least two occasions when feasible.
extension: Apply skill cue review under a new constraint, compare two approaches or perspectives, or teach the idea with an original example without completing another learner’s graded work.
accessibility_and_accommodations: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, manipulatives-based, or demonstrated responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode.
safety_and_privacy: Use respectful, non-shaming language.
Allow a pause, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Check space, footwear, surface, weather, and equipment before movement.
Stop for pain, dizziness, breathing difficulty, head impact, or unsafe conditions and tell an adult.
Score skill, strategy, consistency, and reflection—not body size, weight, speed alone, or comparison with others.

media.fallback: Provide the same information as readable steps, alt text, transcript, tactile/concrete model, or teacher demonstration.

essential_question: How can understanding fitness planning and training principles help us explain, decide, create, or solve something that matters?
learning_objectives: Practice recovery with prompts, feedback, and gradually reduced support.
Use subject-appropriate evidence or representation to communicate understanding of recovery.
Check, revise, or improve work about recovery using stated success criteria.
success_criteria: The learner completes the central task about recovery.
The learner gives evidence, reasoning, a model, or a documented process rather than an unsupported answer.
The learner checks or revises the work and can identify a next step.
materials: unit-specific source, model, manipulatives, safe materials, or approved digital tool

lesson_flow.teacher_or_tutor_action: Present a brief, accessible prompt connected to “recovery.” Ask the learner to notice, predict, estimate, recall, or pose a question before instruction.

Prepare the body, demonstrate the skill, practice at adjustable challenge levels, use safe feedback, and cool down with reflection. Keep the explanation centered on recovery. Name the success criteria and model how to check work or evidence.
Complete two supported examples or source-based tasks about recovery. After each step, ask: “What evidence or reasoning supports that move?” Fade prompts on the second example.
Learner completes a new application of recovery and records both the result and the reasoning, evidence, process, or design choice that produced it.
In one concise response, show or explain the most important idea about recovery; then identify one check that would catch an error or weak claim.

student_activity: Learner completes a new application of recovery and records both the result and the reasoning, evidence, process, or design choice that produced it.
formative_check: In one concise response, show or explain the most important idea about recovery; then identify one check that would catch an error or weak claim.
answer_or_scoring_guidance: Score the stated learning target, accuracy, evidence/reasoning, and revision. Accept multiple valid approaches when they meet the criteria. Do not infer effort, motivation, diagnosis, or character from an error.

adaptive_tutor_routes.action: Return to the smallest prerequisite needed for recovery, model it with a concrete or text-only representation, then retry one fresh item.
Ask the learner to explain or represent why the process for recovery works before continuing.
Confirm the reasoning specifically, offer one varied example of recovery, and avoid unnecessary remediation.
Name the observable pattern neutrally, contrast it with a worked example, and schedule a short same-day or next-session review.
Require accurate independent application plus explanation on a later or different occasion before marking recovery mastered.

mastery_rule: Do not mark mastery from one answer. Use safe participation, skill cues, personal progress, strategy use, and self-assessment without body-size scoring; require accurate independent evidence and successful transfer or retrieval on at least two occasions when feasible.
extension: Apply recovery under a new constraint, compare two approaches or perspectives, or teach the idea with an original example without completing another learner’s graded work.
accessibility_and_accommodations: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, manipulatives-based, or demonstrated responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode.
safety_and_privacy: Use respectful, non-shaming language.
Allow a pause, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Check space, footwear, surface, weather, and equipment before movement.
Stop for pain, dizziness, breathing difficulty, head impact, or unsafe conditions and tell an adult.
Score skill, strategy, consistency, and reflection—not body size, weight, speed alone, or comparison with others.

media.suggestion: Optional diagram, map, worked example, source image, demonstration, or short clip supporting recovery.
media.fallback: Provide the same information as readable steps, alt text, transcript, tactile/concrete model, or teacher demonstration.

parent_or_guardian_visibility: Share the lesson target, completion state, evidence type, and next instructional step. Do not expose raw private reflections, raw answers, voice recordings, or diagnosis language. For safety-critical tasks, record only the needed guardian confirmation.
home_connection: Invite the learner to notice one safe, optional example of recovery in daily life. No purchase, account creation, photograph, or private disclosure is required.
